title: Bacalao en Adobi Dulce (Codfish in Sweet Sauce)
description: A sauce made with egg yolks, tomatoes, and vinegar.
steps: After thoroughly desalting and half-cooking the codfish, cut into regular portions and form a paste with a little flour, two egg yolks, salt and a little oil.
Mix well so that it forms a liquid which when lifted with a spoon makes a thread; if too thick, add a little warm water.
Dip the codfish portions in this paste and fry in oil until golden.
In a pot with butter fry well-peeled and ground tomatoes; add good vinegar, a piece of sugar, and the fried slices of codfish, letting it season.
When the broth has thickened a little, serve.

title: Bacalao en Caldillo de Mantequilla con Queso (Cod in Butter Broth with Cheese)
description: A soup made with butter, cheese, and broth.

ingredients.name: Broth in which cod was cooked
ingredients.sourceText: Broth in which cod was cooked

steps: In a pan over the fire, place four ounces of butter, two of lard and a little oil, and toast there less than an ounce of flour.
When toasted, add a loaf of bread grated into four pieces, and half a pound of aged grated cheese.
Add afterwards, separately, a cleaned garlic head, cinnamon, clove and pepper, all ground together.
Let everything toast, and add a little of the broth in which the cod was cooked, in the quantity necessary so it is neither too thin nor too thick.
When it has boiled well, add three pounds of already-cooked fish.
Once it gives two or three boils, remove and let rest, adding at serving time the cooking oil that is lacking to complete half a quarter of a liter, with what was put in the pan at the beginning.

title: Bagre a la Parrilla (Catfish on the Grill)
description: Prepared with orange or lemon juice, lard, and tomato.
steps: Wash and dry the catfish, add salt, bitter orange or lemon juice and pepper powder, letting it air-dry this way.

Grease some papers with oil, at the same time coating them with lard, and putting on top of them finely chopped pepper, xitomate and parsley, and breadcrumbs; place the fish on them and wrap them in the papers, placing them to cook at gentle heat on the grill.

For the sauce: grind four or five olives according to the amount of sauce you are making; roasted xitomates, a little fried parsley, fried garlic soaked in vinegar, fried chorizo and longaniza and dissolve the ground mixture with oil and juice of raw tomato.

Fry a fine soffritto separately with onion and parsley in greater quantity; when fried, add the ground mixture so that it also fries, adding broth, fine and coarse pepper, clove and cinnamon, vinegar, and three or four drops of Cologne water; season with sufficient salt, and when bringing it to the table place chili peppers and olives on it.

description: Prepared with breadcrumbs, onion, and lard.

title: Bagre en Empanada (Catfish in Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with garlic, orange, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: semolina dough made from fine grain or bran
ingredients.sourceText: semolina dough made from fine grain or bran

steps: Clean the large catfish, remove the bones, and stuff it with cinnamon sticks, pieces of garlic, and pieces of aguacate or orange leaves.

Make a vinegar broth with clove powder, cinnamon and pepper; add a little ground saffron and a few drops of cooking oil; mix everything well, dissolve in generous wine, and place the fish in this infusion from one day to the next.
Form a dough of semolina made from fine grain or bran, and from it make a pastry large enough to contain the fish.

Grease the pastry leaves inside and out with lard so that the edges can be sealed; place the fish in it, pour the broth made with wine over it, close the pastry well forming a seal around the edges, and place it in the oven at a gentle heat.
When it is time to eat it, remove the top from the pastry and place it on the platter carefully so that it does not break.

title: Bagre en Salsa de Xitomate (Catfish in Tomato Sauce)
description: A sauce made with lard, tomatoes, and garlic.
steps: After cleaning the catfish well with ash so that it becomes white, remove the bones and the bones from the center of the head; dry it well with cloth so that it is dry.
Roll it in flour, place it in a pan that has sufficient capacity, add lard and at a low heat that does not burn the lard much, fry it and leave it until it is well browned on the bottom side.

Then turn it carefully so that it does not break, and when it is already browned on both sides, roast some ripe xitomates, grind a little pepper and a bit of garlic, peel the xitomates very well, add the ground pepper and garlic on top and hot lard that is not the one in which the catfish was fried.

Once they have fried a lot with that lard, add a little water, letting it boil until the xitomate breaks down well, and when it has seasoned, pour it over the catfish, and on top raw cooking oil, and let it rest in the heat until time to serve it.

Bone it and season inside with salt and pepper

Cook over two fires for three hours or longer
When ready to serve, drain and untie, remove the skin and cover with gelatin

Let it boil until taking a little with the fingers, it cracks between them

Add almonds, cooked egg yolks, or whatever you wish to glaze, immediately covering the pan so that air cannot reach the syrup
Leave it this way until it cools completely
Break the crust that will have formed on the yolks or items by one side
Drain the honey from them and carefully remove them
Rinse in lukewarm water and let drain

title: Beef Head À lo Natural (Natural Style)

steps: Place a pot of water large enough to turn the head easily over the fire
When water is hot, stir and turn the head in all directions and observe if the hair can be removed
If it can, remove the pot from the fire, take out the head, rub it by hand, and soak in water until all hair is removed
Be careful not to heat the water too much so the skin does not toughen
After this operation, soak the head in cold water for hours
Remove the bones and cook as follows
With the head well scalded and jaws removed, dissolve a handful of flour in a pot or pan with water, bring to a boil and season
Season with salt, pepper, a mixed bouquet of herbs, two onions, carrots, and parsnips
Place the head in this and let cook for three hours or less as needed
When cooked, drain and uncover the brains
Serve with a spicy sauce or simply with oil and vinegar

title: Bizcochos de Santa Inés (Saint Inés Biscuits)
description: A biscuit made with egg yolks, leaven, and flour.

ingredients.name: one pound and four ounces of sugar
ingredients.sourceText: one pound and four ounces of sugar

steps: To one quarter of flour add {{source-1}}, one pound and four ounces of sugar, ten egg yolks and salt to taste; mix and beat a lot with your hands to unite it and allow it to rise well; then add the butter and mix again
Take a handful of leaven, add two handfuls of flour and mix with a little water; if it is stiff, form a ball immediately and cover with a napkin; leave overnight in a vessel
The next day, dissolve the leaven with water until loose and incorporate it with everything else with a little water and knead again in a trough

Knead and work the dough on a table as if washing, break into pieces with a knife and put back in the trough; knead again and when united put on the table and repeat the washing motion, repeating this four or five times so the dough becomes very smooth and soft
Leave in the trough until the next day, then knead once more and mix twice
To shape, weigh six and a half ounces, knead and form sticks half a vara long with proportionate thickness
Place on a board covered with coarse bran so the sticks do not burn
Space them six fingers apart from each other to allow for rising; when risen, cut in half with a knife
Bake in an oven that is not as hot as for bread to prevent burning
Cool, cut into thin slices and return to the oven to toast completely

The flour and sugar powder should have been passed through a sieve to mix well and remove debris
Mix everything well but gently, as this precaution is necessary so the beaten whites do not deflate and fall

Before putting them in the oven, dust them with sugar using a fine sieve
Bake at good heat until they turn a bright yellow

title: Bizcotela a la Francesa (French-Style Sponge Cake)
description: A cake made with syrup, egg white, and orange.

ingredients.name: flour, approximately equal in quantity to the syrup
ingredients.sourceText: flour, approximately equal in quantity to the syrup

Form the mixture into small balls

title: Bobo Guisado (Stewed Bobo Fish)
description: Prepared with fish, olive oil, and peppercorns.
steps: Soak to desalt well and remove the scales
Divide into portions and place on the fire in a pot with water, not cooking all at the same time but one after another; the head should be the last
Place on a platter
Heat olive oil and butter in a pan; add a spoonful of peppercorns to fry a little and mix with the butter in which the bobo fried
Sprinkle the fish with this sauce, adding a little vinegar on top
This stew should be made three or four hours before eating

ingredients.name: one or two tablespoons of strong vinegar

Take care that the bobo fish do not fall apart.

title: Budín Blanco (White Pudding)
description: A pudding made with fish, chicken, and sweetbreads.

ingredients.name: Cow udder cooked in white broth
ingredients.sourceText: Cow udder cooked in white broth

steps: Chop together raw fish meat, chicken breasts, cow sweetbreads, calf brain and carp roe
Grind them very fine or crush in a metate or mortar
Add breadcrumb cooked in milk until it dries
Add as much butter as the amount of meat and breadcrumb used
Add a cow udder previously cooked in white broth and chopped
Add a quarter part of rice cooked in milk
Add the same amount of white onion substance or broth
Add five or six egg yolks, each thing separately, taking care to grind and crush one before adding the other
Fill the intestines, taking care not to fill them too much so they don't burst when cooking
Tie them at both ends
Place them in boiling water for a quarter of an hour
To make sure they are cooked, remove them with a skimmer and prick with a pin
If blood no longer comes out but only fat, it is a sign they are cooked
Let them cool then to roast them on a grill when you want to serve them

description: A pudding made with almonds, egg yolks, and egg whites.
steps: Grind half a pound of almonds without adding water
Separately grind {{source-1}} and sift it
Beat twelve egg yolks and separately beat very well eight egg whites that are mixed with the yolks and the almonds after beating

Grease a pan with butter and a little velorio sponge cake and do not fill the casserole too much because it will puff up
Place in the oven and when it browns on top put a paper on it so it does not burn
With a straw check if it is cooked; when the straw comes out clean it is done
A scraping of orange on top suits it very well

steps: Take one loin of veal and one piece of pork meat, and after cleaning both well, chop and grind them

Place the mixture in a casserole and stir in one soaked loaf of bread, sufficient salt, coarse and fine pepper, chopped onion sautéed with butter, half of finely chopped fat ham, a little melted bone marrow and capers
Mix in eight egg yolks and four egg whites
Beat four more egg whites and add them to the meat, mixing well
Grease a mold with lard, dust it with breadcrumbs, empty the paste into it and cook for three hours in a pot of water, being careful that the water does not penetrate the mold

Add a pinch of pepper, chopped parsley, capers and salt; let everything boil so it seasons well

title: Buey a la Moda (Beef à la Mode)
description: Prepared with beef, bacon, and white wine.

ingredients.name: a piece of veal knuckle without bone
ingredients.sourceText: a piece of veal knuckle without bone

ingredients.name: four to six carrots, cut into pieces

steps: Lard the beef with bacon and season well on all sides with salt and pepper.
Two hours before cooking, soak the meat in white wine.
After one hour, turn the piece so the white wine penetrates both sides.
Place the prepared meat in a pot with a piece of veal knuckle without bone, a bouquet of fine herbs, plenty of chopped onion, and two whole cloves.
Pour one cup of broth over everything and let cook for one hour over low heat.
Turn the meat, add the remaining white wine in which the meat was soaked, along with four to six carrots cut into pieces, and continue cooking.
Use a pot that is not too large so the meat remains always covered with the cooking liquid.
This dish is as good cold and even better than hot. If you wish to serve it cold, it is best to prepare it the day before.

Once prepared, arrange it circularly on the platter, arranging the carrot pieces around it; then pour the sauce over it, which will soon become a jelly. Prepared this way it is an exquisite and elegant dish.

title: Buñuelos Comunes (Common Puffs)

Mix all this in parts and then knead much until it makes bubbles
Cover and put in the sun for two hours

title: Buñuelos de Forma Esponjados (Puffy Molded Fritters)
description: Prepared with lemon, corn, and flour.
steps: To one quarter pound of flour add one quarter pound of milk and a lemon
Use flour that is not sweet, add the milk in small amounts, because if much is added at once it forms many balls
Then heat it in a little butter to put in the bottom of the pan, cook as the previous ones without ceasing to stir and removing the crusts that stick to the pan
Once the dough is cooked, begin to knead it
As soon as you can pick it up with your hand, begin adding eggs one by one; once four or five have been added, add the rest two by two and knead very well so the flour does not become lumpy
Add the corn and one ounce of ground sugar in powder so they come out whole
Then fry them but first let them rest a while

description: Prepared with chiles, ham, and bread.

Clean and dehorn an ox head well, turn it with jaws facing upward
Open with a knife the meat that joins the jaws to expose the tongue
Stuff the tongue with ham and coat the entire center of the mouth with fine salt
Grind the soaked chiles, adding cumin and a bread crumb soaked in vinegar
Dissolve this paste in good vinegar, add plenty of salt
Coat the entire head inside and out with this sauce, repeating two or three times as it dries
Leave it until the next day
On the day to be eaten, make a thicker sauce similar to the first

Grind clean garlic and coat the head with the garlic paste, filling the openings
Cut thin slices of desalted cured beef fat, place some slices inside the mouth, cover all the meaty parts with the rest
Tie the slices with clean thread and put in the oven to cook slowly over gentle heat
When cooked, remove the cured beef fat slices and serve with a chilote sauce
